gap._description: M14 laptop-B round, 2026-10-09 (php-lane). The `gaps` array was empty for a reason that had stopped being current: the only items it ever held were the two #268-family boundaries (PHPD31/PHPD32), which are RULINGS and were promoted out of it. Re-derived from measurement this round rather than re-read from the empty array, the lane has exactly ONE remaining sized item — cross-file `overrides`, which a single-file analyzer cannot state and which PHPD39 deliberately bounds to same-file bases. Its size is now measured instead of asserted: 1,233 cross-file override edges across 755 of 5,094 admitted files, of which 781 have a base leaf declared by exactly ONE admitted file, so the bound is NOT fully explained by leaf ambiguity — those 781 are the part a cross-file index would close. Measured by `npx tsx validation/m14/fixtures/php/override-scope-census.mts` (artifact validation/m14/fixtures/php/override-scope-census.json), whose walker first REPRODUCES the lane's own oracle on the covered subset — 2 same-file edges, matching `script/m14/oracles/php-overrides.ts`, printed as a CONTROL — before it counts the subset nothing covers; a walker that disagreed with the oracle on the covered half could not be trusted about the other. THE SILENT-TYPE QUESTION THAT OPENED THIS ROUND IS NOT A GAP AND IS NOT RECORDED AS ONE: `exports` and `overrides` are both implemented and both fire, `bun script/m14/firing-check.mjs PHP` reports them SILENT because their applicable density in this corpus is 3 sites in 2 files and 1 site in 1 file out of 3,231 — measured, with MISSED 0 on both sides. See PHPD40. Kept as prose so the next reader can tell a ruling that was priced from one that was merely declared.

gaps.type: incoming residual — DECLARED BOUNDARY of per-file analysis, not a missing emission
gaps.status: RULED 2026-10-10 (Lead ruling (a)): ruled with its count, NOT closed
gaps.size: 52,917 of 155,016 `uses` edges (34.1%) are unresolved over the whole admitted population (`npx tsx script/m14/residual-gate.ts --lane php`)
gaps.whyItIsOpen: The targets are generic member names read off a receiver whose TYPE the tree does not state — `request` 1,819, `expected` 1,259, `i` 958, `actual` 761, `node` 545 (whole population, production path). A per-file analyzer knows a receiver's class only for `$this->`, `self::`, `static::`, `parent::` and a NAMED receiver; for `$response->metadata` it knows nothing, and the name itself cannot say which declaration is meant. The owner-qualification pass (cd0c77546) closes exactly the half the file can PROVE — 12,849 edges moved ambiguous -> resolved — and this is the half it cannot. MEASURED, not asserted: only 338 of the 57,729 owner-carrying unresolved edges are this shape in the sense that matters (they carry an owner and the owner's chain is outside the file); the rest have no receiver class at all.
gaps.whatWouldCloseIt: TYPE RESOLUTION — a different instrument (an index-assisted or type-aware pass that knows what a local variable holds). FALSIFIER: if such an instrument lands and this class does not fall, this ruling is refuted and the work reopens. A per-file name rule cannot close it: any name-keyed rule that bound these would be picking among candidates by a rule nobody chose, which is the defect the owner channel was built to remove.
gaps.control: the same probe splits the owner-carrying subset from the receiver-less one, so the boundary is shown to be the RECEIVER's type and not the member name; and the incoming gate's own `ofWhich=0` for `uses` proves the resolutions this lane does make are not tie-break picks

A store pass that marks a row external on 'its target names nothing in the project' is REFUSED BY RULING: the gate would then verify with the same test over the same key space, so the claim would verify by construction, extFAIL would become structurally 0, and the marker would stop carrying information — the laundering `incoming-rule.ts` warns about.

Worse than useless, because THE GATE CHECKS A CLAIM BEFORE THE COUNT: a wrongly-attached claim does not merely fail to help, it BREAKS an edge that resolves today.

decisions.question: PHP property access `$this->balance`, `$obj->name`, `$this->svc->inner` parses as member_access_expression — when is it a READ (uses) vs a WRITE?
decisions.resolution: A member_access_expression that is the FIRST child of an assignment_expression is a WRITE (never a use). A member_call_expression / nullsafe_member_call_expression receiver is a call target, not a read. Everything else inside a method body emits uses -> the member name (isMemberRead). Node identity is compared by byte range because web-tree-sitter re-creates Node wrappers per call (=== never holds). Pure AST, never source-text scanning.

decisions.question: PHP global function calls flood the graph with stdlib edges — filter or keep?
decisions.resolution: PHP_BUILTINS (exported set, ~200 stdlib globals: string/array/type/math/fs/control/preg families) are filtered from call relationships. Method calls (member/scoped/nullsafe) are NEVER filtered — they are user code. The differential oracle imports the analyzer's EXACT set (single source of truth, no hand-duplicated copy).

decisions.question: Where do `use App\Models\User;` imports land — references or imports?
decisions.resolution: imports array ONLY (module = FQN, items = [alias or leaf]). The references relationship kind is reserved for require/include expression file paths (emitInclude). The differential oracle mirrors this split exactly.

decisions.question: Interface inheritance (`interface A extends B, C`) uses the same base_clause node as class extends — how are they distinguished?
decisions.resolution: By container node type: inside interface_declaration, base_clause children are ALL extends targets (interfaces inherit multiple parents); inside class_declaration, base_clause has exactly ONE child = the superclass (extends), and class_interface_clause children are implements. The dead literal 'interface_base_clause' (older grammar) was removed — probe-verified against the pinned wasm 2026-08-30.

decisions.question: AnalyzeContext.overrideCompanion is never populated by production callers — what must analyzers that gate ALL override emission on it do for externally-declared bases?
decisions.resolution: M37.10 ruling (family-wide): the companion is optional enrichment, never a hard gate. Contract: in-file base declaring the method -> verified override (0.95 php/ruby/python/js/perl, 1.0 java/swift Pass-1); companion present -> companion-index resolution (0.85-0.9); otherwise deterministic Pass-3 first-parent guess at 0.5 with reasonCode 'first-parent-guess' and evidence tier 'inferred' — below the patterns.ts 0.7 threshold, counted as heuristic (honest suspicion) by the F5 differential. Gating on the companion alone silently dropped every cross-file override (php, ruby, python, javascript, perl); the inverse overclaim (swift guess at 1.0/structural) is equally a defect. Gated by F9-PROBE-M3710-* probes, per-language external-override fixtures + confidence pins, and 6 regression mutants.

Statements at program scope in PHP scripts, config/bootstrap files, and WP/plugin hook files ($x = new App(); $app->boot(); register_shutdown_function(...)) were silently dropped — the analyzer emitted ZERO edges for them while the differential oracle (a generic walk) derived all of them. decisions.resolution: phpunit is class-heavy: only 4/300 sampled files (1.3%) carry top-level call statements, so the 60-file F5 sample rarely hit the shape — a coverage blind spot exactly like haskell HSD12/CSD1. decisions.question: M37.13: a class may inherit from a DIFFERENT class that shares its leaf name in another namespace — phpmyadmin Setup\FeaturesForm extends User\FeaturesForm, phpunit interface Exception extends \PHPUnit\Exception, class InvalidArgumentException extends \InvalidArgumentException (the SPL builtin). Everything was leaf-collapsed, so the subclass's own name matched the base leaf: fabricated extends Self edges (12 in phpunit, 11 in phpmyadmin), VERIFIED @0.95 self-overrides (16 phpmyadmin, 2 phpunit — the in-file/companion override check matched the class's OWN methods), and `new parent()` -> self. Why did the F5 differential stay green? Both the analyzer AND the oracle leaf-collapsed identically — extends truth fabricated on both sides colluded.
decisions.resolution: Fix (M37.13): heritage-target resolution (heritageTarget). A QUALIFIED base/interface whose leaf equals the declaring class's name keeps its qualification (leading backslash stripped): extends FeaturesForm -> Forms\User\FeaturesForm, and override resolution then runs against the external same-leaf base (M37.10 first-parent guess @0.5/inferred — never verified, never self). A qualified base that qualification CANNOT disambiguate — global single-segment like \InvalidArgumentException — is unresolvable in the leaf graph: NO extends edge and no baseByClass entry (self-loop is always fabrication; family 'wrong edge worse than no edge' precedent, same as unresolvable new parent()). Analyzer metadata.baseClass/extends/implements/enum-implements and oracle derivePhpEdges + deriveTreeEdges heritage all mirror the same helper. Corpus result: self-extends 12->0 (phpunit), 11->0 (phpmyadmin); self-overrides 16->0 / 2->0; differential parity held at 100%/0/0 on both corpora.

Adding instanceof references to php alone would create a family asymmetry in the other direction and require re-pinning both php F5 lanes. Recorded as a measured scope decision, not a hidden skip (both sides silent = differential-consistent 100/0/0).

decisions.question: The php wave (#268 family) declared this a gap: 'HTML/text interpolation segments outside <?php blocks are not symbols; string interpolation internals are opaque'. Is that a gap or a ruling?
decisions.resolution: RULED, not a gap. A `use`d requirement of this lane is a SYMBOL CONTRACT over PHP declarations, and the text outside `<?php ... ?>` is not PHP: it is the template that PHP is embedded in, and its `$var` slots belong to whatever templating engine wrote them (Twig, Blade, Smarty), not to PHP's grammar. Emitting symbols for interpolated HTML would invent PHP declarations that do not exist. The string-interpolation half of the old gap text is separately adjudicated and IS handled: "hello $name" (simple), "{$o->p}" (object/member), and "{$n['k']}" style forms are read for VALUE flow by the in-PHP rules, pinned by php/bare-value-reads and php/header-reads. The old wording conflated two different things — a correct boundary on out-of-PHP text, and an unfinished job on in-PHP interpolation that was in fact finished. Recording it as a `gap` therefore reported finished work as outstanding forever.

decisions.question: The php wave (#268 family) declared this a gap: 'ini directives and shell hash-bang lines are not parsed as symbols or decision points'. Is that a gap or a ruling?
decisions.resolution: RULED, not a gap. `ini_section`/`ini_entry` are .ini FILES parsed by PHP's own INI machinery, not by this analyzer — no PHP declaration exists in them to miss, and the same applies to a `#!` hash-bang line, which is the OS's interpreter directive. The `preprocessor`/`shell_comment` nodes that appear in a .php file are likewise not PHP declarations. Declaring symbols for any of these would put non-PHP constructs into a PHP symbol graph. The grammar emits these node types for these files and the analyzer correctly declares nothing for them, which is a boundary, not unfinished work.

decisions.question: Should the php analyzer emit `exports` edges? ASTEngine.RelationshipType.Exports exists, and src/lsp/graph_request.ts:256 filters on relationship_type IN ('imports','exports') — so after M12.PHP-IMPORTS made php's DEPENDENCIES visible, a php file reports what it needs but not what it offers, which looks like an asymmetry worth closing.
decisions.resolution: SUPERSEDED, AND THE PREMISE WAS FALSIFIED RATHER THAN ARGUED AWAY. This row ruled 'no `exports` kind for php, deliberately', on the grounds that '(1) PHP has no syntax to key on, so any php `exports` edge would have to be SEMANTIC'. PHP does have one: `define()` at FILE LEVEL publishes a name the file does not declare, and it is the only publication form that is not already a symbol in the file. Measured on the admitted population (5,094 files): 57 `exports` edges — 43 resolve uniquely, 14 stay ambiguous — from 60 literal `define()` calls across 20 corpus files (57 at file scope, 11 inside a function body, 1 non-literal name; `defineAtFileScope: 57` is the same number as the edge count, which is what a keyed rule looks like). The row's other two arguments were kept rather than discarded, and they are what shaped the rule: the information is not lost (a `define()`d name is also a file-scope symbol), and a WRONG edge is worse than no edge — which is why a `define()` inside a function, method, closure or class body is EXCLUDED (the `SCOPE` set in `emitDefineExports`; the corpus has 11 such calls, and the mutant `php/emit-nested-define-as-file-export` re-adds them and is CAUGHT by php/define-exports). The label question this row deferred is pinned in the same fixture: a `define()`d name is NOT carried by `contains` (it resolves against the global scope and no node in the file contains it) while a namespace-scoped `const` is, and the mutant that files one under `contains` (`php/file-define-as-contains`) is caught on exactly that discrimination.

decisions.question: The construct census (script/m12/php-construct-census.ts) walked all 4,463 corpus files and found 20 of the grammar's 179 named node types that occur ZERO times in phpunit AND phpmyadmin. Are these unhandled work, or constructs no corpus can exercise?
decisions.resolution: RULED: all 20 were probed by hand against the analyzer, and every one is correct or correctly inert. This closes the last CLAIMED-BUT-NEVER-EXERCISED type, taking that set to EMPTY. Evidence per group: (a) namespace_use_group — grouped `use C\{D, E as F};` emitted NOTHING; FIXED under M12.PHP-GROUPED-USE and pinned by the php/grouped-use fixture. (b) dynamic_variable_name (`$$n`, `${expr}`) — parses clean and emits the correct read of the inner variable name (`uses m -> n`), since the NAME is what is read; the dynamic target is not resolvable from one file and correctly yields no edge. (c) global_declaration — `global $registry, $other;` emits no symbol (the doc already rules globals are never symbols) AND subsequent reads bind correctly (`uses m -> registry`, `uses m -> other`). (d) static_variable_declaration — `static $hits = 0;` binds and its later reads emit `uses`. (e) function_static_declaration — `static function(){}` and `static fn()=>` parse clean. (f) colon_block — the alternative `if: … elseif: … else: … endif;` syntax parses clean and its body statements are read normally. (g) use_instead_of_clause / use_as_clause / use_list — trait adaptation and multi-trait `use` both keep every trait `use` edge, consistent with the model where a trait's methods belong to the trait and are not re-declared on the composing class. (h) var_modifier (`var $legacy = 1;`) — the ONE construct that FAILS to parse, and that is CORRECT: `var` was removed in PHP 7.0, so the pinned 0.24.2 grammar does not accept it, and reporting a parse error for removed dead syntax is the honest outcome. It is absent from both corpora because no modern PHP code contains it. (i) text_interpolation — ruled separately in PHPD31. (j) empty_statement, php_end_tag, goto_statement, named_label_statement, sentinel_error, operation, shell_command_expression, relative_name, disjunctive_normal_form_type — no PHP DECLARATION, so no symbol and no relationship is the correct output; a DNF type or a `goto` label is not a graph node this analyzer claims to model.

decisions.question: PHP 8.3 wrote typed class constants into the language: `const Dep X = 1;` carries a type on the constant. `phpDeclaredTypeRefs` listed the position on its own 'BOUNDARIES, DISCLOSED' comment and emitted nothing for it — but the SPEC claimed `const_declaration` was handled_verified and carried no decision naming typed class constants anywhere in its 33. So the position was documented in a source comment and absent from the adjudication set: an unexamined claim wearing a disclosure's clothes. Is it a boundary, or unhandled work?
decisions.resolution: FIXED, and the finding is that it was never a boundary at all. Probe-verified against the pinned wasm, the grammar carries the type as an ordinary `type` FIELD on the declaration: `const_declaration > const > named_type > name`, a direct sibling of `const_element > name`. That is the same shape, in the same `declaration_list`, naming the same kind of thing, as `property_declaration.type` which the lane has always handled — so a class writing `const Dep X` depends on `Dep` exactly as it does writing `private Dep $f`, and R9's rule ('a declaration that WRITES a type name depends on the type it names') applies without argument. Ruling it out would have manufactured a gap in order to avoid writing the case, so it is HANDLED: the `const_declaration` case in `phpDeclaredTypeRefs` attributes the dependency to the ENCLOSING TYPE, exactly as a property's is. `primitive_type` (`const string S = 'a'`) stays SILENT for the same reason it is silent on a property — the grammar tags it, so it is not a dependency on a userland symbol. WRAPPERS DESCEND: `?Opt` contributes `Opt`, `First|Second` contributes BOTH members, each as its own dependency. RELATIVE TYPES reuse this lane's own probe-verified `new self()` rule: `const self SELF_REF` resolves to the enclosing class, and an unresolvable `parent` emits nothing. FILE-SCOPE CONSTANTS are the one judgement call: a top-level `const Dep TOP = 1;` has no enclosing type and an edge still needs a source, so it is attributed to `global` — the same file-scope owner the read rules use when neither a callable nor a class encloses a position (the trait-use precedent, PHP-O1) — rather than dropped, because a written dependency is not less real for having no owner symbol. THE POSITION IS NOT EXERCISED BY EITHER CORPUS, and that is why it needed a fixture rather than a measurement: both pinned corpora were walked for `const_declaration` nodes carrying a `type` field and MEASURED 243 const_declarations of which 81 are TYPED — and every one of those 81 is a `primitive_type` (`private const string PAGE_HEADER`, `public const int VERSION`). Primitives are silent BY DESIGN, so the position is genuinely exercised 81 times; a NAMED type, the only shape that produces an edge, occurs ZERO times. The absence of `const Dep` references therefore read identically whether the rule worked or did not exist, and the full-extent differential read 100% either way. Pinned by php/typed-class-const (every written-type shape AND every silent case, plus an exact count of 9 references edges so an EXTRA edge cannot hide behind satisfied positive pins) and held by the reverting mutant php/typed-class-const-dropped, CAUGHT by that fixture alone — the isolation is the evidence, because the corpora cannot catch it. Same class as the grouped-`use` defect that 4,139 files and 95,231 edges reported clean while missing the construct entirely: 100% coverage is a statement about the corpus, not about the language.

decisions.question: When recovery MIS-NESTS the remainder of a class body inside the method that precedes a damaged statement, are the declarations it swallowed published? `php/error-recovery` already pins the lane's document-level contract for a file the parser cannot fully read — 'the declarations AROUND it still publish, INCLUDING THE ONES AFTER IT — degradation is PARTIAL, not total' — but it covers the shape where recovery MARKS a node, not the shape where recovery puts it in the wrong parent.
decisions.resolution: FIXED, on a measured shape. `FSharp.Formatting/csharp/MarkdownSharpTests/source/php/markdown.php:910` writes PHP-8-REMOVED curly-brace offset syntax (`$level = $matches[2]{0} == '=' ? 1 : 2;`); the pinned grammar errors there and leaves the enclosing method's body OPEN, so the next twenty real class members become `function_definition` nodes nested inside `method_declaration _doHeaders_callback_setext 905-1575`. Every one of them was invisible to the symbol walk (a declaration inside a body is reached by `walkBody`, which emits reads and pops a scope, never by the symbol pass), while the corpus kept emitting 19 `calls` edges naming them — the whole of the lane's `DECLARED_IN_TREE_NOT_PUBLISHED` residue bar four classifier artifacts, in ONE file. Bisected rather than assumed: replacing that one expression with `$matches[2][0]` moves 11 of 12 members back to direct children of the declaration_list (nested 9 -> 0), while the file's OTHER legacy offset (`switch ($token{0})` at 1560) does not — the two damage sites differ, so the rule is keyed on THIS shape (a named callable sitting directly in a damaged `compound_statement`) and not on 'the file has errors'. THE READING: such a declaration is a MEMBER of the class whose body was swallowed, because the source writes it in the class body between members; publishing it as a global function is the rejected alternative (legal PHP, and this lane models nested functions as file-scope VALUES for resolution — but publication must describe the source, and the rejected reading is pinned by `forbidSymbols` rows on the fixture). THE FIX IS TWO PAIRED HALVES, one predicate asked by both: publish the recovered declarations, and stop the damaged body's walk from descending into them, or every call inside them is emitted twice under two sources — a duplicate no 'at least one' fixture row can see, which is why `expectRelationshipCount` carries that contract. `const`/`property_declaration` are published by the same escape but NOT skipped, because their branches never walk their initialisers and the body walk is the only reader of those values. SCOPE, DECLARED: only DIFFERENT: direct children of the damaged body are recovered; a declaration nested deeper (inside an `if` block inside the damaged body) keeps the old single walk and is still not published — measured residue of that shape in the corpus: 0 edges. MEASURED DELTA over all 5,094 files, production path: `DECLARED_IN_TREE_NOT_PUBLISHED` 24 -> 5, resolved unique 129,020 -> 129,061 (+41 = 19 `calls` that now resolve + 22 new `contains`), edges 350,342 -> 350,364 (+22, all `contains`), published names 21,200 -> 21,222 (+22), and ZERO delta in every other bucket — `calls` 103,190 and `uses` 155,016 unchanged to the digit, which is what separates a fix that resolves edges from one that invents them. Fixtures: `php/recovery-swallowed-members` (authored BEFORE the fix; pre-fix state measured at 4 symbols / 9 edges against 8 / 13 after; the statement FORM had to be probed — a curly offset in a `return` does NOT swallow and a fixture built on it passed before the fix and proved nothing). Mutants, all caught: `php/drop-recovered-members` (the pre-fix state), `php/publish-recovered-members-as-global-functions` (the rejected reading), `php/re-walk-recovered-subtrees` (half the fix).

decisions.question: A named `function` declared INSIDE a callable — `function testProcessRequest(...) {...}` written in a method body, the PHPUnit/Slim test-helper idiom — is unreachable by the symbol walk, because callable bodies belong to `walkBody`, whose job is call/read edges and scope frames and which never publishes symbols. The store therefore ends up WITHOUT a declaration the file contains, while the same file keeps emitting edges SOURCED AT the nested name (`references testProcessRequest -> ServerRequestInterface`, `slim/tests/MiddlewareDispatcherTest.php:73`). Is such a declaration published, and if so as what?
decisions.resolution: FIXED, on a measured population. Whole-population tree walk over all 5,094 admitted php files: exactly 25 `function_definition` nodes whose path to the program root passes through a callable, in 4 files. TWENTY-TWO are `markdown.php`'s recovery casualties (already published as MEMBERS by the recovery escape one layer up, and not nested functions at all — PHPD36); the remaining THREE are this shape and all three are Slim's tests: `AppTest.php:1563` `function handle(...)` inside `testInvokeFunctionName`, `CallableResolverTest.php:30` `function testAdvancedCallable(...)` inside `setUpBeforeClass`, `MiddlewareDispatcherTest.php:32` `function testProcessRequest(...)` inside `setUpBeforeClass`. THE FIRST PROBE WAS WRONG AND THE CORRECTION IS PART OF THE MEASUREMENT: it asked only "is the declaration's parent a `compound_statement`?" and reported 280 hits, 250 of them in ONE file — phpunit's `src/Framework/Assert/Functions.php`, whose 251 assert helpers are guarded by `if (!function_exists('assertSame')) { function assertSame(...) {...} }` at FILE level, which is NOT a scope and which the ordinary walk publishes correctly (measured: 252 symbols, 251 functions). The rule is therefore 'a CALLABLE node sits between the declaration and the program root', and the damage predicate that separates the two populations is the declaration's body parent carrying `hasError` (`damagedBody=true` for all 22 markdown declarations, `false` for all 3 Slim ones). THE DECISION: publish as KIND `function` with the file's NAMESPACE as owner, exactly as a top-level function is published — three independent reasons, each measured. (1) PHP semantics: a named function in a body enters the GLOBAL function table when the enclosing code runs — it is not a local binding the way a Python `def` in a `def` or a Ruby `def` in a `def` is, and against the pinned grammars javascript and typescript publish a nested `function innerHelper() {}` while python and ruby do not. (2) The analyzer ALREADY models it: `collectPhpFileScope` registers every nested named function as a file-scope function VALUE ('Global effects, visible everywhere regardless of nesting'), so the name was already used to resolve bare callables — resolution without publication is exactly the divergence the orphan-endpoint round fixed (PHPD36's sibling). (3) `walkBody` keeps emitting edges sourced at the nested name, so the alternative is a store that carries edges from a declaration it does not hold. THE TWO REJECTED READINGS, pinned as `forbidSymbols` rows on `php/nested-named-functions`: publishing it as a METHOD of the enclosing class (a method may not be declared outside a class body, and the source writes a `function`, so a method symbol describes the shape of the tree — and it would put `contains NestedHost -> nestedHelper` in the store), and publishing it with NO owner (in a namespaced file every top-level function is owned by its namespace, and PHP's global-table name for the declaration is `Fixture\NestedFunctions\innerValue`, not `innerValue`). THE FIX IS A PASS THAT PUBLISHES WITHOUT RE-WALKING: the nested body has already been walked by the enclosing callable's `walkBody`, so re-walking it would emit every call and read inside it a SECOND time under the nested name — a duplicate no 'at least one' fixture row can see, which is why the fixture carries `expectRelationshipCount` rows instead. MEASURED DELTA over all 5,094 files, production path (before/after, same instrument): `publishedNames` 21,222 -> 21,224, `memberPairs` 32,552 -> 32,555 (+3), `edgesTotal` 350,364 -> 350,367 (+3, ALL `contains`), `RESOLVED_UNIQUE` 129,061 -> 129,064 (+3), `perType.contains` 35,109 -> 35,112, `DECLARED_IN_TREE_NOT_PUBLISHED` 12 -> 10, and ZERO delta in every other bucket and every other type — no new ambiguity, no changed source attribution. THE REASON CENSUS now reports 0 endpoints in a class it cannot name on BOTH sides (target defect class 0, source defect class 0, out of 350,367 edges). Fixtures: `php/nested-named-functions` (authored BEFORE the fix; pre-fix state measured at 6 symbols / 10 edges against 8 / 12 after). Mutants, all caught: `php/drop-nested-function-symbols` (the pre-fix state), `php/publish-nested-functions-as-methods` and `php/publish-nested-functions-as-bare-globals` (the two rejected readings), `php/publish-damaged-body-declarations-as-nested-functions` (the damage guard removed — the reading that would make markdown.php's 22 recovered members both members and globals). KNOWN AND UNCHANGED, recorded with its count rather than pinned as correct: call/read edges inside a nested function's BODY are attributed to the enclosing callable. It is one edge on the fixture (`calls registerHelper -> decorate`, written in `nestedHelper`'s body) and it is an ATTRIBUTION decision, not an unexplained endpoint — the enclosing callable is published, so the census is silent about it by construction.

decisions.question: Rule 1 for `exports` was a SPELLING test: the callee had to be exactly the bare name `define`. Two spellings name the same function, and PHP's own resolution rules say which ones — is the FULLY QUALIFIED `\define(...)` a publication the file makes, and can a spelling test ever be complete?
decisions.resolution: FIXED, and HOW it was found is the part worth keeping. A whole-population define-audit (validation/m14/fixtures/php/exports-probe.mts, the `defineAudit` block) built the DENOMINATOR the label had never had — every `define`-family call in the 5,094 admitted files, split by callee RESOLUTION | scope | name-literalness, with every shape key PRE-SEEDED at 0 so that a zero is a measurement rather than an absent key — and read 58 tree-implied file-scope literal-name publications against 57 emitted edges. The missing one is phpunit's `tests/end-to-end/generic/_files/auto_prepend_file.php`: ONE file-scope `\define('AUTO_PREPEND_FILE_LOADED', true);`, in a file whose entire purpose is that PHP's `auto_prepend_file` publishes a constant every later script can read, refused for its SPELLING alone. PHP's rules decide the three spellings apart (manual, Name resolution rules: 'Fully qualified names always resolve to the name without leading namespace separator'; 'Relative names always resolve to the name with namespace replaced by the current namespace'; and the fallback to global functions/constants is stated for UNQUALIFIED names, so a relative name does NOT fall back): `\define` is the global function unconditionally, `namespace\define` is a strict current-namespace lookup, `Other\define` is a userland function. Rule 1 is therefore a RESOLUTION rule accepting `define` and `\define`, and `metadata.calleeShape` records which one ('bare' | 'absolute-fq'). PRICED rather than assumed: qualified `Other\define` 0 occurrences over the population; relative `namespace\define` 0; the aliased `use function define as pub` — which DOES publish, because an unqualified name is translated through the function import table — 0, recorded as a boundary rather than half-implementing an import table for one callee; `class_alias`/`function_alias` 0 on both the old and the new measurement (the probe's P3 overturn condition is not met); and NO file in the population declares its own `define`, which is the only way the bare-name test could have been unsound. THE ORDER OF EVIDENCE is what makes this a measurement: (1) the fixture `php/define-exports` and its expectation were extended FIRST, with four new negative shapes (`Other\define`, `namespace\define`, a nested `\define` and the aliased form), and the suite read FAIL on the missing symbol, the missing export and all four relationships; (2) the analyzer fix made the suite 27/27 pass; (3) a revert mutant `php/drop-absolute-fq-define-publication` filters `exports` edges by `metadata.calleeShape` — GENERICALLY, with no hardcoded target, so it cannot silently stop matching — and is CAUGHT by that fixture (`mutant-check.mts`: 16 mutants caught, 0 survived, clean baseline 0 problems); (4) the whole-population before/after (reason-census, `sampled: false`, same instrument) changed exactly the fields that follow from the one edge: `edgesSeen` 350,367 -> 350,368, `symbolsPublished` 40,266 -> 40,267, `exports` 57 -> 58 (`resolved:unique` 43 -> 44), `targetClasses/resolved:unique` 115,660 -> 115,661, `sourceClasses/source:global` 29,891 -> 29,892, `incoming/declarations` 40,266 -> 40,267, `reachedByAtLeastOneResolvingEdge` 21,144 -> 21,145, `reachedAndNamedByNothing` 17,350 -> 17,351 — with `namedButReachedByNone` UNMOVED at 14,371 and `defectRows`/`unexplainedTotal` still 0. An instrument correction belongs to the finding: the audit's own classifier had to be made REACHABLE before it could report a zero — `member_call_expression` and `scoped_call_expression` leave the `function` field NULL and carry the member name in a `name` field, so `$o->define(...)` / `Foo::define(...)` can never be classified by a test on the callee FIELD's type (measured by parsing all four spellings side by side); written the CLOSED IN THE SAME ROUND, and the closure is a second artefact rather than a sentence: the oracle `script/m14/oracles/php-exports.ts` was written from PHP's resolution rules (sharing no code with the analyzer), imported and registered in `script/m14/differential.ts`, and `exports` was admitted to php's compared-label set — so `rel-type-coverage-gate` now lists php in NO un-audited row at all (`emitted` == `audited` == the same ten labels, DERIVATION list empty). decisions.question: M14 laptop-B round, SECOND criterion: `npx tsx script/m14/incoming-gate.ts php php 60` reads FAIL (135 ambiguous + 2,483 unresolved of 3,257 edges, 0 marked external). The contract says an external target is a DECLARED EXCEPTION and not a defect, but only if the lane MARKS it. Which of the 2,483 are external, which are defects, and can this lane mark its way to the gate's PASS?
decisions.resolution: THE SPLIT IS MEASURED, THE MARKER WAS INVISIBLE, AND THE PASS IS UNREACHABLE FOR PHP BY MARKING — each part separately, because only the first two are fixable in this lane. (1) THE SPLIT. `npx tsx validation/m14/fixtures/php/incoming-census.mts 60` rebuilds the gate's own stride sample and its own key space (name + qualifiedName per repo, the gate's `classifyEdge` imported rather than re-implemented) against a key space built from the UNSAMPLED admitted population (5,094 `.php` files, 9 repos, 21,225 distinct names + 33,318 qualifiedNames from 4,944 files carrying symbols). It reproduces the gate's verdict EXACTLY — 135 ambiguous + 2,483 unresolved of 3,257 edges, printed as a self-check — so the split below is a split of the gate's own number: (a) 1,325 edges name declarations that ARE in the corpus and are unresolved only because the run's 60-file stride does not contain the declaring file — a BUDGET artefact, not an analyzer defect (the gate's own header says a stride sample cannot answer a file-scoped question, and running the whole project (`php php 0 --repo=phpunit`) moves resolution from 639 of 3,257 (19.6%) at 60 files to 33,427 of 133,468 (25.0%), because 80,726 of those edges are ambiguous against a whole-project key space and no sample size fixes that); (b) 1,158 edges name nothing anywhere in the admitted corpus, of which 35 are php-src names by the analyzer's own table (`phpInternalKind`). SHAPE, and it is the decisive fact for what marking can buy: of the 2,483 unresolved targets, 2,478 have NO DOT AT ALL — 2,321 bare and 157 backslash-qualified FQNs — so `targetOwner` returns null for every one of them, and the remaining 5 are dotted targets that only LOOK owner-shaped: they are FILE PATHS (`smartypants.php`, `__DIR__/../src/FirstPartyClass.php`, …) whose extension merely looks like a member separator. (2) THE MARKER WAS INVISIBLE. `labelExternalTargets` has always written `metadata.external = <kind>` — a STRING — while the gate's `EXTERNAL_KEYS` test is `md[key] === true` (or a non-empty array) (`script/m14/incoming-rule.ts:249-258`), so every php-src label this lane ever emitted read as an edge carrying NO claim: measured on the gate's sample, 88 unresolved edges carried the label as a string and 0 as `true`. FIXED, additively: `md.external = true` with the kind moved to `md.externalKind`, the boolean spelling the family already uses (`real-lua-analyzer.ts:2023`) and the one the contract states. MEASURED EFFECT, before -> after on the same command: unresolved 2,483 -> 2,395 (-88, exactly the number of labelled edges), and the verdict now names the residual class instead of hiding it — `FAIL — 135 ambiguous + 2395 unresolved of 3257 edges; 88 external claim(s) unverifiable (0 verified + 88 unverifiable external)`. Regression evidence for the change: all 30 php fixtures PASS (`npx tsx script/m14/run-fixtures.ts --lang php`) and all 23 php mutants are CAUGHT with a clean baseline (`npx tsx validation/m14/fixtures/php/mutant-check.mts`). (3) WHY A PASS IS UNREACHABLE FOR PHP, and this is a finding about the arbiter's RULE, not about this analyzer: `verifyExternalClaim` (`script/m14/incoming-rule.ts:467-478`) verifies an owner-claim by looking up `targetOwner(tgt)`, which is everything before the LAST DOT — a dart/java convention. PHP's namespace separator is a backslash and its member targets are bare, so for every one of the 2,478 bare targets `targetOwner` returns null and the claim lands in `externalUnverified`, which the verdict's own PASS condition requires to be zero (`bad === 0 && externalUnverified === 0 && bindingUnverified === 0`). A php lane that marked every genuinely-external edge PERFECTLY would therefore still FAIL — with `N external claim(s) name no identifier-shaped owner` — and the only php target that IS owner-shaped is a file path, whose 'owner' is the basename before `.php`, so the one verify path that can fire for php is an accident of file extensions. This is reported rather than worked around: no key in `EXTERNAL_KEYS` changes it (`binding`/`remoteRef`/`importProjectFile` are all refuted or unverifiable for these spellings), and marking names the analyzer cannot prove external would be laundering, which the contract forbids. The narrow, checkable fix belongs in the rule (verify the TARGET itself when it has no owner — the same `decls === 0` fact the owner lookup uses, and it can still never raise `resolved`), and that file is the Lead's, so it is named here as the next step.

decisions.question: M14 laptop-B round 2: the gate's `ambiguous` column is the one number that did not move — 135 at the 60-file sample scope and 80,726 at whole-project scope. Is it a fixable identity defect, or a language property?
decisions.resolution: RULED IRREDUCIBLE IN THIS LANE'S SCOPE, classified with counts the way the powershell lane classified its 219 so the two rulings can be read side by side. `npx tsx validation/m14/fixtures/php/project-scope-census.mts phpunit 60` adds an OWNER dimension to the key space (a declaration's identity is (file, owner), not just the file) and sorts every ambiguous name into four classes: multiFile (declarations in more than one file), oneFileDiffOwner (one file, different owners), oneFileSameOwnerDiffKind (one file, one owner, more than one kind — a method and a property sharing a name), sameKind (one file, one owner, one kind, multiple declarations). SCOPE A, the gate's own sample: 135 edges over 20 distinct names — multiFile 11 names/68 edges (50.4%), oneFileSameOwnerDiffKind 8 names/66 edges (48.9%), oneFileDiffOwner 1/1 (0.7%), sameKind 0. SCOPE B, whole phpunit (133,468 edges): 80,726 ambiguous edges over 1,876 names — multiFile 1,661 names/78,184 edges (96.9%), oneFileSameOwnerDiffKind 214 names/2,541 edges (3.1%), oneFileDiffOwner 1/1, sameKind 0. `sameKind` IS THE ONLY CLASS AN IDENTITY DEFECT COULD HIDE IN AND IT IS EMPTY AT BOTH SCOPES — that emptiness is the falsifier for the ruling, and it is why the column is not chased. The mass is PHP's own semantics: `$obj->member` and `$obj->run()` dispatch on a VALUE whose type one file cannot know (`__construct` alone is declared 654 times in 653 files), and 73.0% of ambiguous edges (58,901) name MEMBER-ONLY names. The column is a key-space fact as much as an analyzer one: the same edges read 135 against a 60-file key space and 80,726 against the whole project, with nothing about the analyzer changing between them. THE REDUCTION PATH EXISTS AND IS OUT OF SCOPE, stated rather than half-done: emitting owner-qualified member targets (`Owner.member`) where the receiver's owner is knowable would collapse the multiFile mass, but the differential's oracle (`script/m14/differential.ts` `derivePhpEdges`) emits BARE member targets, and the store's resolution plus this lane's fixtures pin that spelling — changing the analyzer alone would manufacture differential mismatches no lane in this scope can fix. Recorded so the next round starts from the price rather than rediscovering it.

decisions.question: M14 laptop-B round 2: the unresolved column reads 2,395 at the 60-file sample scope and 14,878 at whole-project scope. How much of the sample figure is key-space BUDGET rather than defect, and what is left at project scope once the budget is removed?
decisions.resolution: BOTH SCOPES BESIDE EACH OTHER, each self-checked against the gate, because one number alone misleads in both directions. SAMPLE SCOPE (`php php 60`, 3,257 edges): 2,395 unresolved after claims (73.5% of edges), 2,483 with claims ignored, and of those 2,483 a measured 1,325 (53.4%) are KEY-SPACE BUDGET — they name declarations that ARE in the corpus, and are unresolved only because a 60-file stride over 5,094 does not contain the declaring file. PROJECT SCOPE (`php php 0 --repo=phpunit`, 133,468 edges): 14,878 unresolved after claims (11.1% of edges) plus 4,437 external-verified, and 19,315 with claims ignored. The budget share at project scope is ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION (the whole project is in the key space), and the raw 19,315 splits into exactly four measured buckets with no defect in it: 172 path-shaped targets (a FILE reference — `require_once 'A.php'` — never a defect), 0 declared in this project (this is where a resolution defect would appear; a 2-row version of it was the PROBE's flaw, corrected and recorded in the doc), 2,138 declared in another admitted repo (external to this project, inside the corpus), and 17,005 declared nowhere in the corpus, of which 4,241 carry a php-src name over 346 names. READ TOGETHER: the sample inflates the unresolved RATE by 6.6x (73.5% of edges at 60 files against 11.1% at whole-project scope) and 53.4% of its raw column is pure key-space budget, which is why the lane reports both scopes and never the sample alone. The remaining project-scope residue is 2,138 + 17,005 edges that name something the project does not declare; the analyzer can prove externality for the 4,241 php-src-named ones (it carries the table) and CANNOT for the rest (one file cannot know whether a name is declared by a sibling file), so they stay unmarked and reported rather than guessed at.
